0.long_answer: Hydrocephalus can lead to focal neurological deficits due to an increase in intracranial pressure that may compress various cranial nerves. The cranial nerve responsible for the movement of the muscle responsible for outward gaze is the abducens nerve (cranial nerve VI). This nerve controls the lateral rectus muscle, which abducts the eye. When the abducens nerve is damaged, it can result in an abducens nerve palsy, characterized by difficulty in eye abduction and resulting in double vision and impaired lateral gaze.
